services.title: Business Setup Services
services.intro: Choose the help you need before, during, or after forming a U.S. company.
sections: Form an LLC
Prepare your business information, review the state filing instructions, and compare what providers actually include. [Explore LLC Formation](services/llc-formation/)
Find a registered agent
Compare the annual renewal cost, document handling, and state coverage before choosing a provider. [Explore Registered Agent Services](services/registered-agent/)
Apply for an EIN
Review the information to gather and the official IRS application routes. [Explore EIN Assistance](services/ein-assistance/)
How to compare a quote
Ask for the state filing fee, provider charge, and optional items on separate lines.
Confirm which services renew and whether renewal is automatic.
Ask what happens if the filing needs a correction or the provider cannot accept your application.
Choose by where you are now
Still deciding: compare formation states and identify where you actually plan to operate.
Ready to form: gather the information the state asks for and request an itemized formation quote.
Already formed: check whether you need to appoint or change an agent, apply for an EIN, or prepare for a renewal.
Compare the first two years

Write the provider setup charge and government filing fee in a first-year column. Put agent renewal, optional address service and applicable state filings or taxes in a second-year column. Ask for the billing schedule before choosing.
Keep your records together
Retain your quote, accepted filing, agent agreement, EIN confirmation if applicable, and a list of recurring dates. Use the [setup resources](resources/) to build your own checklist.

services/llc-formation.title: LLC Formation
services/llc-formation.intro: Prepare your information, understand the filing process, and see what to check before ordering a formation package.
sections: Before you file
Identify the state where you plan to operate and check whether registration there or in another state may be necessary.
Check the state naming rules and verify availability with the filing office.
Confirm your registered agent and the addresses the filing form requires.
Ask for an itemized quote
Separate state filing fees from the service charge. Ask which documents the provider prepares, whether the registered agent is included, and how long any introductory pricing lasts.
After filing

Keep the filed formation document and confirmation. Review your operating agreement, EIN needs, licensing, and annual obligations. Start with the [SBA guide to registering your business](https://www.sba.gov/business-guide/launch-your-business/register-your-business).
Related services
Review [Registered Agent Services](services/registered-agent/) and [EIN Assistance](services/ein-assistance/).
What an itemized estimate should show
Government filing fee, with any expedite charge shown separately.
Provider preparation fee and which documents are included.
Registered agent, address or mail services, and how each subscription renews.
How the provider handles corrections, cancellations and refunds.
Business addresses and documents

Check how the form distinguishes the principal office, mailing address and registered office. Ask the provider whether any address included in the package can be used for the specific purpose you need.
Your formation timeline

Ask the provider to separate its preparation time from the state's processing time. After acceptance, download the filed document and verify the legal name and filing date before using either on other applications.

services/registered-agent.title: Registered Agent Services
services/registered-agent.intro: Understand what a registered agent handles and what to ask a provider before choosing one.
sections: What the agent does

A registered agent receives official papers for the business and must be located in the state of registration. Confirm which documents the provider scans, forwards, or stores. See the [SBA registration guide](https://www.sba.gov/business-guide/launch-your-business/register-your-business).
What to compare
Ask for the first-year price and the rate when the service renews.
Ask how quickly notices appear and whether forwarding costs extra.
Confirm whether the price includes only agent service or a separate business mailing service.
Ask how to cancel or change agents and which filing is required.
If you are switching
Review your state's instructions, coordinate the effective date with the new agent, and keep the state's confirmation. [Browse State Guides](states/)
Registered agent vs. business mailing service

A registered agent is designated to receive official documents. If you also need mail scanning or a business address, ask whether these are separate services and confirm the kinds of mail the provider accepts.
Questions to send a provider
What does the service cost in the first year and at renewal?
How will I be alerted about an official document, and when will it be available?
Are physical forwarding, extra recipients or a change-of-agent filing included?
How do I cancel the subscription after the state accepts a replacement agent?
Keep the appointment and renewal records
Keep the appointment confirmation with the business records. Review the delivery email, account access and renewal date before assuming notices will reach the right person.

services/ein-assistance.title: EIN Assistance
services/ein-assistance.intro: Gather the details for your federal Employer Identification Number application and review your options.
sections: Before applying
Confirm the legal name and formation details on your documents. Determine who the responsible party is and check which details the IRS requires for your application.
Apply through the IRS

The IRS issues EINs directly at no charge. The application method can depend on where your principal business is located and the responsible party’s information. Check the [official IRS EIN instructions](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/employer-identification-number) before choosing a method.
If you use a paid service

Ask which support the fee buys, who will prepare and submit the application, and how you will receive the confirmation. Read the [IRS Form SS-4 instructions](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/iss4) before authorizing anyone to act on your behalf.
Online and international applications

Check the IRS online tool's eligibility requirements first. It asks for the responsible party’s SSN or ITIN and is for eligible applicants with a principal place of business in the United States or a U.S. territory. If the principal place of business is outside the United States, follow the international application instructions on the [official IRS EIN page](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/employer-identification-number).
Prepare before submitting
Use the name the state accepted rather than a trade name in the legal-name field.
Check that the address, entity type and reason for applying match your records.
Use the current [Form SS-4 instructions](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/iss4) if using a route that calls for the form.
Keep the IRS confirmation and avoid submitting another application while you are following up on the first.
Cost and scope of paid help
Ask what the assistance fee covers, whether you need to sign an authorization, and how the service will deliver the IRS confirmation. The IRS itself issues EINs without an application fee.

states.title: U.S. State Guides
states.intro: Compare the questions to answer before choosing a state and open the official filing information.
sections: Featured state guides
[Wyoming LLC guide](states/wyoming/)
[Delaware LLC guide](states/delaware/)
[Texas LLC guide](states/texas/)
Other states
Use the [50-state selector](#setup) on the homepage to build a checklist. Use your state filing office for the current forms and fee schedule.
Decide based on how you operate
Consider where you have an office, employees, or regular business activity.
Compare the cost to form, annual filings or taxes, and renewal charges for a registered agent.

Ask whether you may also need to register in another state where you operate. The [SBA registration guide](https://www.sba.gov/business-guide/launch-your-business/register-your-business) covers this question.
Compare the full cost of a state

Start with the formation fee and annual state requirements. Add the cost of a registered agent, optional address services and any registration needed in a second state. Use each filing office’s current fee schedule.
Example: operating in another state

If you are considering one state for formation and another for your day-to-day business, look up both states' requirements before choosing. The [SBA registration guide](https://www.sba.gov/business-guide/launch-your-business/register-your-business) explains how foreign qualification may apply.
What the directory does
The three featured guides link to state-specific filing instructions. Selecting another state from the directory opens a general checklist with that state preselected.

states/wyoming.title: Wyoming LLC Setup
states/wyoming.intro: Find the Wyoming filing starting point and see what to review before and after forming.
sections: Prepare the filing

Use the Wyoming Secretary of State’s [business forms page](https://sos.wyo.gov/Business/Forms.aspx) to find the LLC Articles of Organization and related instructions. Review registered agent and address requirements before filing.
Budget for the next year
Look up the state's annual report requirements and current fees. If you hire a registered agent, ask for their renewal cost separately from the state's charges.
Before choosing Wyoming

If you will operate elsewhere, use the [SBA registration guide](https://www.sba.gov/business-guide/launch-your-business/register-your-business) to check whether another registration may be needed. [Compare other states](states/)
Annual report timing

Wyoming generally makes the annual report due on the first day of the anniversary month. For example, an LLC formed in May would use May 1 as its recurring report date. Confirm the due date for your business through the [Wyoming Secretary of State’s business FAQ](https://sos.wyo.gov/FAQS.aspx?root=BUS).
Check the official documents

See the state's [LLC Articles of Organization](https://sos.wyo.gov/Forms/Business/LLC/LLC-ArticlesOrganization.pdf), including registered agent information. Use the [Wyoming business portal](https://wyobiz.wyo.gov/Business/Default.aspx) to look up the filed entity and current filing options.
Wyoming setup checklist
Check the proposed name and review the state’s address fields.
Confirm your agent appointment and the provider’s renewal price.
Keep the Articles and the state's filing confirmation.
Record the annual report due date and any separate provider renewal date.

states/delaware.title: Delaware LLC Setup
states/delaware.intro: Start with Delaware’s official formation instructions and review costs beyond the initial filing.
sections: Prepare the filing

Delaware's [formation guide](https://corp.delaware.gov/howtoform/) walks through choosing an entity and a Delaware registered agent. Review the Certificate of Formation and the filing options it links to.
Review ongoing obligations
Check Delaware’s current LLC tax guidance before paying a provider. Ask for the first-year and renewal costs so the initial filing price does not obscure ongoing expenses.
Compare with your operating state
Check whether activities in another state could trigger a second registration. [Compare other states](states/)
Plan for the annual LLC tax

Delaware’s Division of Corporations says LLCs pay an annual tax by June 1 and do not file an annual report for this tax. Review the [Delaware Division of Corporations FAQ](https://corp.delaware.gov/faqs/) for the amount and rules before setting your calendar.
Prepare before requesting a quote
Check the LLC name and confirm your Delaware registered agent.
Ask if the service supplies an accepted copy of the Certificate of Formation.
List the annual state tax and the agent renewal separately.
Keep the file number

Once the entity is registered, keep the file number with the formation documents. Use the [Delaware entity status options](https://corp.delaware.gov/onlinestatus/) when you need to check a record or find out how to request official proof of status.

states/texas.title: Texas LLC Setup
states/texas.intro: Review the Texas filing forms, registered agent details, and follow-up requirements before ordering a service.
sections: Prepare the filing

Find the Texas LLC Certificate of Formation on the [Secretary of State forms page](https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms_boc.shtml). Review the instructions for the registered agent, registered office, and business information.
Check post-formation requirements
Review [Texas Comptroller franchise tax guidance](https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/) and relevant local permits for your activities. Put applicable filing deadlines on your calendar.
Ask for a complete quote
Compare the state filing fee, preparation cost, and registered agent renewal before selecting a package. [Browse provider profiles](providers/)
Use the current Form 205 instructions

The [Texas Secretary of State’s Form 205 instructions](https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/instructions/205.shtml) walk through the entity name, registered agent and office, governing authority, and organizer details. Check those fields before completing a provider's intake.
After registration

Keep the accepted Certificate of Formation and verify your address and governing details. Check the [Texas Comptroller’s franchise tax page](https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/) for rules that apply to your reporting year and business.
Texas setup checklist
Identify who will manage the LLC before preparing Form 205.
Confirm registered agent consent and the registered office details.
Check any local permits or tax registrations relevant to your activities.
Record the state obligations and provider renewal dates separately.

providers.title: U.S. Formation Providers
providers.intro: A starting list for researching providers. Check eligibility, package details, and current prices directly before ordering.
sections: How to compare
Record the initial service price, state fees, renewal rate, state coverage, and eligibility in the same order for each provider. Use the official links above for the latest details.
Use the same questions with every provider
Does this package cover my formation state and accept someone in my country of residence?
What is the total due today, including state fees and any expedited processing?
Which add-ons renew, at what rate, and how do I cancel them?
How will I receive the accepted filing and other official documents?
Collect comparable quotes

A package can show a low setup price while charging separately for the agent or other services. Ask for a dated quote that separates one-time costs from recurring charges, and confirm how long the price applies.
Provider listing policy
The directory links to provider-operated websites. The order of the cards is a directory order. Check eligibility, refund terms, and scope directly with the provider before ordering.

how-it-works.title: How Renz Works
how-it-works.intro: Go from a general idea to a checklist you can use when researching or choosing a service.
sections: 1. Choose a state
Select a formation state or leave it undecided. The [State Guides](states/) explain where to start.
2. Pick the task
Choose LLC formation, registered agent services, EIN assistance, or help deciding.
3. Review your checklist
The homepage form builds a brief checklist in your browser. Use it to gather information and prepare questions for a provider.
4. Confirm details with the provider
Before paying, confirm eligibility, total initial price, renewal terms, and what the company will deliver. See [provider profiles](providers/).
Example: starting a Wyoming LLC

Select Wyoming and LLC Formation. Use the checklist to verify the name, confirm an agent, and review the filing instructions. Then open the [Wyoming guide](states/wyoming/) for state sources and the annual report timing.
Example: changing an agent

Select the state where your LLC is already registered and choose Registered Agent. Ask the replacement about effective dates and document handling, and check the state’s change-of-agent requirements before cancelling the existing service.
What you can do after the checklist

Open the [service guide](services/) for details, read the relevant official filing page, or contact a provider for a written quote. The checklist is a planning tool and the site does not submit your selections as a request.

resources.title: Business Setup Resources
resources.intro: Checklists and official starting points for U.S. founders preparing to file or compare services.
sections: Business setup checklist
Before filing: choose a state, check the proposed business name, and confirm agent arrangements.
After filing: keep the accepted document, check EIN and licensing needs, and record annual deadlines.
Before paying a provider: confirm what’s included, how long a quote applies, and what renews.
For founders outside the U.S.

Ask each provider whether it accepts applicants in your country of residence and what verification it requires. Check the [IRS EIN page](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/employer-identification-number) for application options. Verify bank or payment-provider eligibility separately.
Official starting points
[SBA: Register your business](https://www.sba.gov/business-guide/launch-your-business/register-your-business)
[IRS: Employer Identification Numbers](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/employer-identification-number)
[State filing guides](states/)
Questions for a provider inquiry

Use this starting point: “I’m considering a [state] LLC. Please confirm applicant eligibility, the total first-year cost with state fees, the registered agent renewal price, any optional charges, and what documents I will receive.”
Records to keep
Keep the state’s filing receipt and accepted formation document together.
Save the registered agent agreement and its renewal terms.
If applicable, keep the IRS EIN confirmation with your company records.
Record annual state obligations, optional subscription renewals, and local permit dates.
Compare sources
Use state and federal agencies for filing rules and deadlines. Use the provider’s written quote and terms for package contents, pricing, renewal, cancellation and refund details.

about.title: About Renz
about.intro: Renz gives founders practical starting points for U.S. company formation, registered agent services and EIN preparation.
sections: What Renz covers

Renz focuses on U.S. business setup. The site brings together service explanations, questions to ask providers, state filing links, and checklists for common tasks. It is written for people planning a new company or handling a next step for an existing one.
Who the guides are for
First-time founders who want to understand how a formation quote is put together.
Owners comparing a registered agent’s renewal price and document delivery.
Founders outside the United States gathering questions about eligibility, documents and EIN application options.
How we organize the information

State and federal agency pages support the sections about filing and application rules. Provider websites are linked alongside the directory cards so you can ask the provider to confirm pricing, eligibility, and what a package includes.
How to use the provider directory

Compare upfront charges, renewal costs, state coverage, eligibility and what you will receive. The order in the directory is a listing order. Ask each provider the same questions and keep its latest written quote with your records.
What the checklist does
Pick a state and service and Renz will generate a short planning checklist in your browser. You can then open the relevant guide, consult the official filing office or contact a provider directly.
Keep reading

Start with the [Renz Blog](blog/) for practical examples and the [state directory](states/) for filing links. The [Contact page](contact/) explains how to prepare a setup question and where to direct it.

contact.title: Contact Renz
contact.intro: Plan what to include when you ask for help with a setup question.
sections: Prepare your question
Have your intended formation state, service, and current stage ready. If you are comparing providers, include the name of the package and the price you were quoted.
Request status
Direct messaging is not available in this version. You can [build a setup checklist](#setup) now.
What to include in a question
The state you are considering, or where the company is already registered.
The service you need and whether you have already filed any documents.
The provider name and package you are comparing, if applicable.
One or two specific points you want clarified. Leave out sensitive numbers and documents.
Find the right source

For filing status or a state form, start with the official office linked in the [state guides](states/). For EIN application questions, see [official IRS guidance](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/employer-identification-number). For package billing or a refund, contact the provider that issued the invoice.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: How Renz handles checklist choices, routine website requests, and visits to linked providers or government agencies.
sections: Scope
This notice covers the Renz website, including the blog, service and state guides, provider directory, and setup checklist. A site reached through an external link has its own privacy practices.
Information used by the checklist

The checklist uses the formation state and the service you choose to prepare a list in your current browser. The checklist does not submit those selections as a message or keep its own saved copy. Its fields do not request names, email addresses, tax numbers, documents, or payment details.
State selections in page links

The state directory can include a state name in the URL so the checklist opens with that state selected. The requested URL can appear in browser history and ordinary hosting logs. The link does not carry a name or a personally identifying application number.
Hosting and access

When a page is loaded, the hosting service may process routine request information, such as the requested URL, browser information and IP address, to deliver and protect the site. If a private preview asks you to sign in, the host manages that sign-in under its own terms. Renz’s checklist does not receive your password.
Cookies and browser storage

The public-facing Renz pages and checklist do not set their own advertising cookies or save a checklist in browser storage. A host may use its own access or security technology, such as when signing in to an owner-only preview.
Links to other websites

The site includes links to formation providers and government agencies. Once you visit another site, check its privacy information before entering personal, company or payment details. Renz does not receive an application you submit on those sites through the provider directory.
Messages and sensitive documents

The current Contact page is informational and does not accept messages or file uploads. Do not put tax IDs, passports, payment information or official documents into links or use them as search terms on Renz.
Using the site and reading this notice

You can use the formation guides and blog without submitting a checklist. See the [Contact page](contact/) for other ways to find the right source for a question. Review this notice when a new feature changes how the site handles information.

blog.title: Renz Blog
blog.intro: Practical articles for forming a U.S. business, choosing providers, and staying organized after filing.

blog/compare-llc-formation-quotes.title: How to Compare LLC Formation Quotes
blog/compare-llc-formation-quotes.intro: Compare what you’ll pay to start and what you’ll pay again next year before choosing a formation package.
sections: Start with the same filing
Ask each provider for a quote for the same entity type and state. Request standard processing on each quote if speed is not a priority. This keeps expedited fees from distorting the comparison.
List government and provider charges separately
Record the state filing fee and optional expedite charge.
Record the provider preparation charge and what documents it includes.
Add the registered agent, mail forwarding or address service if you need them.
Check whether a quoted discount expires or requires an automatic renewal.
Compare the second year as well
Write down every renewal separately, including any state annual report or tax that applies. A $100 lower setup quote can cost more over two years when the annual package is more expensive.
What to ask in writing
Try: “Please confirm the total due today, the total you expect me to pay again next year, which services renew automatically, and how I can cancel each one.” Save the reply alongside the quote.
Work through a two-year example

These figures illustrate the comparison and aren’t provider prices. Quote A: $190 to start and $220 in year two, for $410 total. Quote B: $250 to start and $120 in year two, for $370 total. Quote A starts $60 lower, but Quote B costs $40 less over two years. Compare the same services before deciding.
Read the terms behind the price
Ask whether the quote covers a registered agent for a full year or a shorter promotional period.
Check if the provider charges for an accepted copy of the state filing or for specific delivery methods.
Find out what happens to the provider fee and state fee if an application is withdrawn or rejected.
Where to verify filing requirements

Use the [SBA business registration guide](https://www.sba.gov/business-guide/launch-your-business/register-your-business) and your state filing office for government requirements. For package terms, use the provider’s quote. [Open the Renz provider directory](providers/).

blog/registered-agent-checklist.title: What to Ask Before Choosing a Registered Agent
blog/registered-agent-checklist.intro: A practical checklist for state coverage, renewal costs, and delivery of official documents.
sections: Confirm the appointment

Confirm that the provider covers the state where your entity is registered. Ask for the exact information your state form requires and check whether the filing fee for appointing or changing the agent is included.
Test the document workflow
Ask how soon documents typically appear after receipt.
Check whether notifications can go to more than one authorized person.
Ask what mail the provider accepts and what it costs to forward physical documents.
Confirm how to access previous documents if you move to another provider.
Check renewal and optional services
Ask when the agent subscription renews and what it costs. If you also need a business mailing address, ask for a separate quote and check the permitted uses of that address.
If you already have an agent
Ask the new provider how to coordinate the change and when the appointment takes effect. Check the state’s filing instructions, then keep confirmation of the change with your business records.
Ask for a real example of the process

Give the provider a scenario: “If you receive a document with a response deadline on a Friday, how will you notify me and where will I find the document?” Ask how to add a backup contact and whether there is any additional cost.
Set reminders before you renew
Record both the state’s filing deadlines and the date the agent subscription renews.
Confirm how to change the account email if staff or ownership changes.
Keep a copy of the appointment confirmation and the cancellation terms outside the provider dashboard.
Official starting point

See the [SBA registration guide](https://www.sba.gov/business-guide/launch-your-business/register-your-business) for the role of a registered agent. [Read the Renz registered agent guide](services/registered-agent/).

blog/ein-application-options.title: EIN Options for U.S. and International Applicants
blog/ein-application-options.intro: Find the official IRS application route and gather the information needed before you apply.
sections: Start with the IRS eligibility guidance

The IRS’s online application is for eligible applicants whose principal business is in the United States or a U.S. territory. The IRS also publishes a separate path for applicants whose principal place of business is outside the United States. Check the current instructions before you begin.
Prepare your information
Use the name shown on the accepted formation document.
Confirm your entity type, mailing address, and reason for applying.
Identify the responsible party and use the current Form SS-4 instructions if your route calls for the form.
Keep your IRS confirmation with the state filing.
When paying for help

There is no IRS charge to issue an EIN. If a provider charges to help with your application, ask what it will prepare, whether you will need to sign an authorization, and how it will send you the confirmation.
Common problems before you apply
Check your approved legal name against your formation document instead of copying the name from a draft order.
Check which application route the IRS directs you to based on the principal place of business and the responsible party’s information.
If an application is pending, use the IRS follow-up instructions before submitting again.
Save and use the confirmation

Keep the IRS confirmation with the company’s formation records and limit access to the people who need it. If it is lost, consult the [IRS EIN confirmation guidance](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/employer-identification-number) for current options.
Official IRS links

Read the [IRS EIN application options](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/employer-identification-number) and [Form SS-4 instructions](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/iss4). [See the Renz EIN guide](services/ein-assistance/).

blog/after-llc-formation.title: What to Do After Your LLC Is Formed
blog/after-llc-formation.intro: A starting checklist for company records, renewals, and official filings after the state accepts your LLC.
sections: Make a company records folder

Save the accepted state filing, receipt, agent details, operating agreement if applicable, and EIN confirmation if issued. Verify the legal name and spelling across the documents before using them for another application.
Build a calendar before renewals arrive
Find and note the state reporting or tax deadlines that apply to your entity.
Record the registered agent renewal date and any address-service subscriptions.
Check whether your business activity requires city, county or state licenses and when they renew.
Verify deadlines in the right place

Rules differ by state and entity type. Start with the [Wyoming Secretary of State FAQ](https://sos.wyo.gov/FAQS.aspx?root=BUS), the [Delaware Division of Corporations FAQ](https://corp.delaware.gov/faqs/) or the [Texas Comptroller franchise tax page](https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/) as relevant to your company.
Separate the tasks by owner
Put the registered agent's delivery contact and backup contact in writing.
Decide who monitors state renewal dates and who retains receipts and confirmations.
Give your tax preparer or accountant the company records they request through an appropriate channel.
Create a recurring review

Review deadlines and provider renewal charges before the business’s anniversary month. If your address, agent or business activities have changed, check the state’s instructions and update the relevant records.
If you operate in another state

Check whether the state where you operate requires a separate registration. The [SBA registration guide](https://www.sba.gov/business-guide/launch-your-business/register-your-business) outlines how to look up foreign qualification. [Browse the Renz state guides](states/).

blog/choose-an-llc-state.title: How to Choose a State for Your LLC
blog/choose-an-llc-state.intro: Compare where you will operate, what state filings apply, and the total cost of maintaining your company.
sections: Start where you will do business

List where the LLC will have an office, employees or regular operations. Ask the relevant filing offices how they apply their registration rules to your facts. Forming in one state may lead to a second registration in a state where the business operates.
Build a two-year comparison
List the filing fee and any optional expedited processing.
Add the registered agent price for each state where the business needs an agent.
Check likely annual reports, taxes or related charges with each state office.
Record any registration, record request or certificate fee associated with operating in another state.
Apply it to a simple scenario

If you plan to run the business from Texas but are considering forming in Wyoming, check what it would take to operate in Texas before comparing quotes. Include both states’ requirements in your estimate if the business needs both registrations.
Use official sources

Read the [SBA business registration guide](https://www.sba.gov/business-guide/launch-your-business/register-your-business) and compare the [Wyoming](states/wyoming/), [Delaware](states/delaware/) and [Texas](states/texas/) starting guides.

blog/llc-vs-corporation.title: LLC or Corporation? Questions to Ask Before Filing
blog/llc-vs-corporation.intro: Compare how you plan to run the business, bring in owners, raise money, and manage recurring obligations.
sections: Ownership and management

An LLC generally refers to its owners as members. A corporation issues shares to shareholders. Decide who will own the company, who will make day-to-day decisions, and how you will document changes in control.
Plans for investment

If you expect to raise outside capital, ask prospective investors and your adviser whether they have requirements for the structure. Compare those needs with the ownership arrangements you want today.
Separate state structure from federal tax treatment

Formation is a state-level process. Federal tax treatment depends on the entity and its elections. Check IRS guidance for the facts of your company before choosing a structure solely because you heard it is taxed a particular way.
Before asking a provider to file
List current and future owners and how you expect to split responsibilities.
Ask about what governance documents are included and which recurring filings apply.
Confirm the entity type on your order before paying.
Official starting points

See the [SBA business structure guide](https://legacy.sba.gov/business-guide/launch-your-business/choose-business-structure) and the [IRS business structures overview](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/business-structures).

blog/us-company-from-abroad.title: Starting a U.S. Company from Abroad
blog/us-company-from-abroad.intro: A pre-order checklist for non-U.S. residents comparing formation providers and related services.
sections: Check service eligibility first

Give the provider your country of residence and ask whether it accepts applicants there. Request a written list of acceptable identification and address documents. Check what happens to your payment if verification is unsuccessful.
Keep addresses and roles clear
Ask which company addresses each filing or service needs and whether a registered agent package includes a separate mailing service. Confirm what kinds of mail can be accepted, scanned or forwarded.
Plan EIN, banking and payments separately

Read the [IRS application options](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/employer-identification-number) before ordering EIN assistance. Separately ask the bank or payment company you plan to use about its country, document and identity requirements before relying on that account for your business.
Ask about reporting before you form

A tax adviser familiar with U.S. cross-border businesses can help you determine which federal, state and home-country obligations apply. Share the proposed ownership, location and business activity when getting advice.
Checklist before paying
Ask the formation provider for a dated quote and confirm residence eligibility.
Check the official filing process and expected records.
Keep the formation, EIN and account-opening steps on separate checklists.

blog/annual-compliance-calendar.title: Build an Annual Compliance Calendar for Your LLC
blog/annual-compliance-calendar.intro: Track state requirements, registered agent renewal, and related business deadlines in one place.
sections: Start with the state’s rules

Check the state where you formed and any additional states where the LLC is registered. Identify which obligations are tied to a calendar date, which depend on the formation date, and which depend on your business circumstances.
See why deadlines differ

Wyoming generally ties its annual report to the first day of the anniversary month. Delaware lists June 1 as the deadline for its annual LLC tax and says LLCs do not file an annual report for that tax. Texas publishes franchise tax reporting guidance separately. Check the official links before adding deadlines to your calendar.
Record state charges and subscriptions separately
Keep one calendar entry per filing or renewal.
Record the agency or provider, what is due, and who is responsible.
Add a reminder ahead of each deadline and retain the receipt or confirmation.
Review the entries if you change agents, move or register in a second state.
Official state resources

Use the [Wyoming Secretary of State FAQ](https://sos.wyo.gov/FAQS.aspx?root=BUS), [Delaware Division of Corporations FAQ](https://corp.delaware.gov/faqs/) and [Texas Comptroller franchise tax guidance](https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/) as applicable.
